why: Two full dates 91 days apart in the SAME calendar year. Nothing else in the corpus reaches this path: of eleven pairs only two carry a full date on both sides, and one is 0 days apart (inside the first band) while the other trips the 1970-epoch guard, whose DATE_EPOCH_MISMATCH_FLOOR clamps the result and masks the fall-through entirely. So the corpus passed unchanged through eidr-core 0.24.1's fall-through fix -- the THIRD consecutive cycle it could not exercise the thing being changed (eidr-core, 2026-08-31). The lesson: extra precision may CONFIRM within the bands but must never invent similarity that year-level data would not support, so a full-date pair may never outscore its year-only equivalent. `field_quality_max` on release_date is what pins it -- under the 2.8.0/0.24.1 inversion these two dates scored 1.00, ABOVE the 0.70 that 31 days apart scored, because the last band sits below the year table's gap-0 anchor and falling past the bands jumped back up.
